can compile — analyze sources and emit the compile artifact

Usage: can compile [--format=json|text] [--catalog=PATH] FILE.can...

Text lists one emitted module path per line; json prints the artifact envelope. Analysis or emission errors (E6006/E6007/E6008) report diagnostics instead of an artifact.

Exit codes: 0 emitted, 10 errors reported, 2 tool failure.

can check — analyze sources and report diagnostics (full pipeline over the producer catalog; result is complete=true)

Usage: can check [--format=json|text] [--catalog=PATH] FILE.can...

Catalog order: --catalog PATH, CAN_CATALOG, ./can-catalog.json, ./packages/values/dist/catalog.json (emit it with `npm run catalog` in packages/values). Without a catalog, builtin names do not resolve.

Exit codes: 0 clean, 10 errors reported, 2 tool failure.

can lint — analyze sources, then run lint rules over the checked program (recommended rules; warnings/informational only, never blocking)

Usage: can lint [--fix] [--format=json|text] [--catalog=PATH] FILE.can...

Analysis errors report diagnostics with exit 10 and no lint findings. On a clean analysis the lint findings print as the diagnostic envelope (exit 0: warnings never block). With --fix, machine fixes are computed and reported (JSON gains a sorted `fixes` array; text gains one `fix` line per fix); nothing is written.

Exit codes: 0 findings-or-clean, 10 analysis errors reported, 2 tool failure.

can fmt — format sources canonically

Usage: can fmt [--check] [FILE.can...|-]

Formats each file in place, writing only files that change. With no operands, or `-`, reads stdin and writes the formatted text to stdout. `--check` writes nothing and lists the files that differ instead. Parse failures print the machine-JSON diagnostic envelope on stdout and write nothing. Exit codes: 0 clean, 10 errors or differences reported, 2 tool failure.

can explain — print a diagnostic catalog entry

Usage: can explain [--format=json|text] CODE

Exit codes: 0 printed, 2 unknown code (E7003) or bad usage.

can lsp — run the language server over stdio

Usage: can lsp

Speaks Content-Length JSON-RPC; see the transport module docs.
Stdin EOF shuts the server down with the lifecycle exit code; a
shutdown request followed by the exit notification exits 0, exit
without shutdown exits 1.

Exit codes: 0 clean shutdown (shutdown+exit, or stdin EOF), 1 exit without shutdown, 2 tool failure.

can policy — dump the declared policy surface (roles, model policies/invariants, operation gates)

Usage: can policy [--format=json|text] [--catalog=PATH] FILE.can...

Reads the checked program and prints the policy surface in source order.
Exit codes: 0 clean, 10 errors reported, 2 tool failure.

can docs — generate the localized internal declaration reference

Usage: can docs [--locale=TAG] [--out=PATH] [--format=json|text] [--catalog=PATH] FILE.can...

Analyzes sources, extracts the frozen reference model v1 and pipes it as JSON through stdin to the `can-platform docs` renderer (fixed args, no shell), which selects description variants through the shared TS locale resolver and writes Markdown. Without --out the Markdown goes to stdout; without --locale the renderer uses the app default locale plus source fallback. --format shapes diagnostics only, never the Markdown. Analysis errors report diagnostics (exit 10) with no reference output and no file write; a missing runtime/renderer or a failed render is tool error E7004. --out refuses `.can` paths and input files: authored sources are never overwritten. The reference never runs business handlers or examples.

Exit codes: 0 rendered, 10 errors reported, 2 tool failure.

can completions — print a shell completion script

Usage: can completions bash|zsh|fish

Prints the completion script for every `can` command, flag and
operand to stdout; eval it or install it (see docs/install.md).

Exit codes: 0 printed, 2 unknown shell or bad usage.

can help — show help

Usage: can help [COMMAND]

With no command, prints the global help (`can --help`). With a
command, prints that command's help (same as `can <COMMAND> --help`,
except run|test|build|deploy|activate pass a trailing `--help`
through to can-platform, so `can help <COMMAND>` — like
`can --help <COMMAND>` — is the way to see their `can`-side help).

Exit codes: 0 printed, 2 unknown command.

can run — thin lane-7 entry (passthrough to can-platform)

Usage: can run [ARGS...]

Execs `can-platform run` with argument passthrough when the lane-7
producer is installed, else reports missing-producer error E7004.
Everything after the subcommand passes through verbatim, flags
included (`can run --help` asks the platform tool; use
`can help run` or `can --help run` to see this text). `can` never embeds a second
platform engine. Override search with CAN_PLATFORM_BIN. The child
process exit code passes through; a signal-killed child maps to
exit 2.
